columns.name: ElseGroup
columns.label: Else Group
columns.hint: Allows building grouped conditions - all entries belonging to the same condition (same SourceType, SourceGroup and SourceEntry) that share the same number in ElseGroup, define one group.
columns.description:
Allows building grouped conditions - all entries belonging to the same condition (same SourceType, SourceGroup and SourceEntry) that share the same number in ElseGroup, define one group. The **entire condition** is met when **any of its groups** is met (logical OR). The **group** is met when **all of its entries are met** (logical AND).

Example:

Two conditions with the same SourceType, SourceGroup and SourceEntry but with a different Condition, the first one has ElseGroup = 1 and the second has ElseGroup = 2, this creates a Logical OR.

Two conditions with the same SourceType, SourceGroup and SourceEntry but with a different Condition, both has ElseGroup = 1, this creates a Logical AND.

tables.name: creature_addon
tables.label: Creature addon
tables.description: The [creature_addon](../world/creature_addon) and [creature_template_addon](../world/creature_template_addon)  tables define different things that are applied on creatures when they are loaded. These "different things" can be for example to have the creature be mounted, to have it emote something, to have it display an aura effect, etc. Through the use of the fields in this table, many things can be changed about the outward visual appearance of the creature. The creature_template_addon table affects all creatures with that creature template ID while the creature_addon table affects individually spawned creatures (so that two creatures using the same template can look different). > Note: A [creature_addon](../world/creature_addon) record will override a [creature_template_addon](../world/creature_template_addon) record should they overlap on the same creature.

columns.name: point_2
columns.label: Point 2
columns.hint: These values are used to set leaderGUID pre ending path points for memberGUID's where the path is a straight return path and memberGUID's should not crossover to other side of leaderGUID on direction change.
columns.description:
These values are used to set leaderGUID pre ending path points for memberGUID's where the path is a straight return path and memberGUID's should not crossover to other side of leaderGUID on direction change.

If your leader has a path like the one below where he moves to point 5 then back to 1 you would set point_1 = 4 and point_2 = 8 on the memberGUID. If the memberGUID is at angle 90 up to point 5 it will switch to angle 270 for the return trip. This is only needed to keep creatures on the correct side. these values can be left at 0 for creatures following directly behind leaderGUID or any creatures in a circular path. 

```
1     2     3     4    5
-----<--------->------
       8    7      6
```

columns.description:

tables.name: creature_template_addon
tables.label: Creature template addon
tables.description: The [creature_addon](../world/creature_addon) and [creature_template_addon](../world/creature_template_addon)  tables define different things that are applied on creatures when they are loaded. These "different things" can be for example to have the creature be mounted, to have it emote something, to have it display an aura effect, etc. Through the use of the fields in this table, many things can be changed about the outward visual appearance of the creature. The creature_template_addon table affects all creatures with that creature template ID while the creature_addon table affects individually spawned creatures (so that two creatures using the same template can look different). > Note: A [creature_addon](../world/creature_addon) record will override a [creature_template_addon](../world/creature_template_addon) record should they overlap on the same creature.

columns.description: This is the [creature_template.entry](../world/creature_template#entry) to which the script is linked to.

columns.name: GroupID
columns.label: Group ID
columns.hint: If there is more than one of the same entry (more than one text the creature says), this column is used to choose if it is a random say or an ordered list.
columns.description: If there is more than one of the same entry (more than one text the creature says), this column is used to choose if it is a random say or an ordered list. If a creature has got more than one say text to be shown in a given order, it must be incremented for each new matching entry (ex. 0, 1, 2, 3...). If there is only one entry or only one group, this value should be 0. If there are multiple groups of texts, this value stays the same within the group while the id increments within the same group.

columns.name: ID
columns.label: ID
columns.hint: Entry for each group of texts.
columns.description: Entry for each group of texts. This is the unique identifier when entry (creature) is the same and **GroupID** is unchanged, it must be incremented (ex. 0, 1, 2, 3...). A creature say will be randomly selected from this list based on the groupid it belongs to.

columns.description: A value from 1–100 that represents the percentage chance that this text will be executed.

columns.label: Event Entry
columns.description: Entry of the event. Keep it as low as possible and prevent making holes in the list. Higher the max id is, the more memory will be used to store the event data.

columns.name: start_time
columns.comment: Absolute start date, the event will never start before
columns.label: Start time
columns.hint: Absolute start date of the event.
columns.description: Absolute start date of the event. The event will start occurring only if the local time at the server is after the one set here.

columns.name: end_time
columns.comment: Absolute end date, the event will never start after
columns.label: End time
columns.hint: Absolute end date of the event.
columns.description: Absolute end date of the event. The event will stop occurring if the local time at the server is after the one set here.

columns.name: occurence
columns.comment: Delay in minutes between occurences of the event

columns.hint: Number of minutes between 2 occurrences of the event.
columns.description:
Number of minutes between 2 occurrences of the event. (2880 = 2 days, 1440 = 1 day, etc).
> Note: Setting this to 0 will crash the server.

columns.name: length
columns.comment: Length in minutes of the event
columns.label: Length
columns.hint: Number of minutes the event will last after the start of the occurrence.
columns.description:
Number of minutes the event will last after the start of the occurrence. (2880 = 2 days, 1440 = 1 day, etc)
This value must be lower than occurrence one or the event will never stop.

(e.g.: Darkmoon Faire has a preparation stage where it sets up.)

min.: 1 - max.: MAX_HOLIDAY_DURATIONS (10)

columns.name: description

columns.description: String containing the name of the event displayed in console each time it starts or stops.

columns.description: This is a boolean field that determines if this game event is a world event or not. 0 = normal event, 1 = world event. If you want conditions for the event, you ***need*** to choose world event. For the world event to work, you need to at a minimum, populate [game_event_condition](../world/game_event_condition) and [game_event_quest_condition](../world/game_event_quest_condition).

columns.name: announce
columns.comment: 0 dont announce, 1 announce, 2 value from config
columns.label: Announce
columns.hint: 0: don't announce 1: announce description to world 2: use Event.Announce setting from config
columns.description:
* 0: don't announce
* 1: announce **description** to world
* 2: use `Event.Announce` setting from config

tables.name: game_event_condition
tables.label: Game event condition
tables.description: This table contains conditions to meet for the specified game event to be completed. Also contains the world state fields used for reporting the given conditions progress and/or max required value. This table will do absolutely nothing if you have not set the event to be a [world event](../world/game_event#world_event).

columns.name: condition_id
columns.label: Condition id
columns.hint: This is the condition ID for this particular world event condition.
columns.description: This is the condition ID for this particular world event condition. It is an arbitrary number, and you can have multiple conditions for each world event. It links to [game_event_quest_condition.condition_id](../world/game_event_quest_condition#condition_id).

columns.name: req_num
columns.label: Req num
columns.hint: This is an arbitrary value that determines when this condition is met.
columns.description: This is an arbitrary value that determines when this condition is met. For example, if you set this value to 1000, and there is only one quest in [game_event_quest_condition](../world/game_event_quest_condition) that will fulfill this condition, and it increases this condition by 100 (by setting the [num](../world/game_event_quest_condition#num) field to 100), then you would need to have your players complete 10 of that quest to fulfill this condition.

columns.name: max_world_state_field
columns.label: Max world state field
columns.hint: This is the world state update field number sent to the client that is used to report the maximum number of needed points in order to satisfy this condition.
columns.description: This is the world state update field number sent to the client that is used to report the maximum number of needed points in order to satisfy this condition. It can be found in [gossip texts](../world/npc_text) referenced with `$XXXXw` where `XXXX` is the world state number that will be sent when that gossip is displayed. If you are doing a custom event, you can pick any number you want that isn't in use, it just needs to match the custom text that you put into the [npc_text](../world/npc_text) table.

columns.name: done_world_state_field
columns.label: Done world state field
columns.hint: This is the world state update field number sent to the client that is used to report the number of accumulated points so far for this condition.
columns.description: This is the world state update field number sent to the client that is used to report the number of accumulated points so far for this condition. It can be found in [gossip texts](../world/npc_text) referenced with `$XXXXw` where `XXXX` is the world state number that will be sent when that gossip is displayed. If you are doing a custom event, you can pick any number you want that isn't in use, it just needs to match the custom text that you put into the [npc_text](../world/npc_text) table.

columns.name: description
columns.label: Description
columns.hint: Arbitrary text field describing this condition.
columns.description: Arbitrary text field describing this condition.

columns.name: Text
columns.label: Text
columns.description:
The actual text. The message in this field will be shown as the text on a page.

You can use certain placeholders that will be filled in in-game:
* `$B`: line break
* `$N`: the players name
* `$R`/`$r`: player race in upper case first/lower case
* `$C`/`$c`: player class in upper case first/lower case
* `$Gmale:female[:reference];`: _male_ and _female_ can be replaced with any synonym you want and one will be chosen depending on the reference. 
_:reference_ is optional and can be `r` (the players race), `c` (the players class) or if omitted the players chosen gender.
* `$4022W`: references a worldstate and will be replaced with it's current value. (here BATTLEFIELD_WG_WORLD_STATE_DEFENDED_H (4022) is chosen as an example)
* `$Tstring1:string2;`: becomes the players PVP rank. (the provided strings are apparently ignored by the client)

tables.label: Pool members
tables.description: This table holds the contents of pools created in [pool_template](../world/pool_template).

columns.name: spawnId
columns.label: Spawn Id
columns.hint: type = 0: creature guid type = 1: gameobject guid type = 2: pool entry

columns.name: chance
columns.label: Chance
columns.hint: The explicit percentage chance that this entity will be spawned.
columns.description:
The explicit percentage chance that this entity will be spawned.

If the pool spawns just one entity (max limit = 1 in the respective pool_template), the core selects the entity to be spawned in a two-step process: First, only the explicitly-chanced (chance > 0) entity of the pool are rolled. If this roll does not produce any entity, all the entity without explicit chance (chance = 0) are rolled with equal chance.
If the pool spawns more than one entity, the chance is ignored and all the creatures in the pool are rolled in one step with equal chance.

In case the pool spawns just one entity and all the entity have a nonzero chance, the sum of the chances for all the entity must equal to 100, otherwise the pool won't be spawned.

columns.label: Description
columns.hint: This field usually names the creature/gameobject corresponding to the guid and mentions which spawn point it is.
columns.description:

* Spawn Point 4 - Tin Vein

columns.name: QuestDescription
columns.label: Quest Description
columns.hint: Fulltext quest description under heading: _Description_ You can use certain placeholders that will be filled in in-game: $B: line break $N: the players name $R/$r: player race in upper case first/lower case $C/$c: player class in upper case
columns.description:
Fulltext quest description under heading: _*Description*_

You can use certain placeholders that will be filled in in-game:
* `$B`: line break
* `$N`: the players name
* `$R`/`$r`: player race in upper case first/lower case
* `$C`/`$c`: player class in upper case first/lower case
* `$Gmale:female[:reference];`: _male_ and _female_ can be replaced with any synonym you want and one will be chosen depending on the reference. 
_:reference_ is optional and can be `r` (the players race), `c` (the players class) or if omitted the players chosen gender.
* `$4022W`: references a worldstate and will be replaced with it's current value. (here BATTLEFIELD_WG_WORLD_STATE_DEFENDED_H (4022) is chosen as an example)
* `$Tstring1:string2;`: becomes the players PVP rank. (the provided strings are apparently ignored by the client)

If value is 0 then it has not been parsed yet.

If value is above 0 then it has been parsed with WDB files from that specific [client build](/en/database/335/auth/realmlist#gamebuild).

* **PrevQuestID** < 0: Contains the parent quest id, that must be active before this quest can be started.

columns.label: Next Quest ID
columns.hint: NextQuestID > 0: Contains the next quest id, if PrevQuestID of that quest is not sufficient.
columns.description:
* **NextQuestID** > 0: Contains the next quest id, if **PrevQuestID** of that quest is not sufficient.
* **NextQuestID** < 0: Contains the sub quest id, if **PrevQuestID** of that quest is not sufficient. If quest have many alternative next quests (class specific quests lead from single not class specific quest) field **PrevQuestID** in next quests can used for setting this dependence.

columns.name: ExclusiveGroup
columns.label: Exclusive Group
columns.hint: ExclusiveGroup > 0: Allows to define a group of quests of which only one may be chosen and completed.
columns.description:
* **ExclusiveGroup** > 0: Allows to define a group of quests of which only one may be chosen and completed.
E.g. if from quests 1200, 1201 and 1202 only one should be allowed to be chosen, insert 1200 into ExclusiveGroup of all 3 quests.

* **ExclusiveGroup** < 0: Allows to define a group of quests of which all must be completed and rewarded to start next quest.
E.g. if quest 1000 dependent from one of quests 1200, 1201 and 1202 and all this quests have same negative exclusive group then all this quest must be completed and rewarded before quest 1000 can be started.

> Note: All quests that use an **ExclusiveGroup** must also have entries in [quest_pool_template](../world/quest_pool_template) and  [quest_pool_members](../world/quest_pool_members) in order for the core to choose one randomly. See the examples section for examples.

columns.name: BreadcrumbForQuestId
columns.label: Breadcrumb For Quest Id
columns.hint: Breadcrumb quests exist for the sole purpose of guiding the player to a new zone or subzone to quest in.
columns.description:
Breadcrumb quests exist for the sole purpose of guiding the player to a new zone or subzone to quest in. They are often given by NPCs upon completing the previous quest hub, as well as Hero's Call Boards, Warchief's Command Boards, and the Adventure Guide. Often there are multiple breadcrumb quests followed by the same follow-up quest, and normally they are mutually exclusive, meaning that accepting one breadcrumb quest will make all the others leading to the same location unavailable. Also, normally completing the follow-up quest will make any breadcrumb quests leading to it unavailable, whether or not they were completed.
**BreadcrumbForQuestId** is the follow up [quest_template.ID](../world/quest_template#id)

tables.name: skill_discovery_template
tables.label: Skill discovery template
tables.description: This table controls the so called "discovery" system of learning spells. This system is used by the alchemy and inscription profession and controls the chance for a player to "discover" another recipe while creating items with known recipes.

columns.name: spellId
columns.label: Spell Id
columns.hint: The recipe Spell ID that has a chance to be automatically discovered.
columns.description: The recipe [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id) that has a chance to be automatically discovered.

columns.name: reqSpell
columns.label: Req Spell
columns.hint: reqSpell = 0: Any recipe spell can trigger the discovery reqSpell > 0: Must use a specific recipe to trigger the discovery (e.g.: Cauldron of Major Arcane Protection will only be discovered while using Major Arcane Protection Potion).
columns.description:
* **reqSpell** = 0: Any recipe spell can trigger the discovery
* **reqSpell** > 0: Must use a specific recipe to trigger the discovery (e.g.: [Cauldron of Major Arcane Protection](aowow.trinitycore.info/?spell=41458) will only be discovered while using [Major Arcane Protection Potion](https://aowow.trinitycore.info/?spell=28575)).

columns.name: reqSkillValue
columns.label: Req Skill Value
columns.hint: The minimum points requirement in profession skill to discover spellId.
columns.description: The minimum points requirement in profession skill to discover **spellId**.

columns.name: chance
columns.label: Chance
columns.hint: The chance, in percent, that a recipe has of being automatically "discovered", whether by any recipe use or by the specific recipe use defined in reqSpell.
columns.description: The chance, in percent, that a recipe has of being automatically "discovered", whether by any recipe use or by the specific recipe use defined in **reqSpell**.

columns.description: The [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id) that creates the item.

columns.name: requiredSpecialization
columns.label: Required Specialization
columns.hint: The character must have the Spell ID specified here learned to have a chance at triggering the extra item proc.
columns.description: The character must have the [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id) specified here learned to have a chance at triggering the extra item proc.

columns.name: additionalCreateChance
columns.label: Additional Create Chance
columns.hint: The chance that the player will create an additional item.
columns.description: The chance that the player will create an additional item.

columns.name: additionalMaxNum
columns.label: Additional Max Num
columns.hint: The number of extra copies that can be created.
columns.description:
The number of extra copies that can be created.
**additionalCreateChance** is rolled for each attempt, until failure or reaching **additionalMaxNum**.

tables.name: skill_fishing_base_level
tables.label: Skill fishing base level
tables.description: This table controls the minimum skill level required in SKILL_FISHING (356), to fish in a certain area with 100% success. > Note: This does not affect fishing from fishing nodes.

columns.name: skill
columns.label: Skill
columns.hint: The minimum skill points in fishing required to fish in the area without receiving trash.
columns.description:
The minimum skill points in fishing required to fish in the area without receiving trash.

If the player is less skilled, the chance to fish successfully is as follows:
* `chance = MAX(1; (playerSkill / areaSkill)^2 * 100)`

tables.name: smart_scripts
tables.label: SmartAI scripts
tables.description: > Manual editing smart_scripts table can be tedious and difficult, for easier writing scripts you can use additional TrinityCore tools like [WoW Database Editor](https://github.com/TrinityCore/WoWDatabaseEditor/).

columns.name: entryorguid
columns.label: Entryorguid
columns.hint: source_type = 9: invoking entryorguid 100 (+i, if multiple timed action lists are set) entryorguid > 0: entry of the creature / game object / etc.
columns.description:
* **source_type** = 9: invoking **entryorguid** * 100 (+i, if multiple timed action lists are set)
* **entryorguid** > 0: entry of the creature / game object / etc.
* **entryorguid** < 0: guid of the creature / game object / etc.

values.name: Creature
values.comment: entryorguid is a creature entry (positive) or spawn guid (negative)

columns.name: id
columns.label: Id
columns.hint: Incremental id bound to each entryorguid + source_type (0, 1, 2, ...).

columns.name: link
columns.label: Link
columns.hint: Simple event linking; Example: if id = 0 and link = 1; id 1 will only be able to occur if id = 0 was triggered.
columns.description:
Simple event linking;
Example: if **id** = 0 and **link** = 1; **id** 1 will only be able to occur if **id** = 0 was triggered.

columns.name: Difficulties
columns.label: Difficulties
columns.hint: Comma-separated list of difficulties where only the event can occur.
columns.description:
Comma-separated list of difficulties where only the event can occur. `''` means everywhere.
> **Examples**:
> * '' → Everywhere
> * '0' → Open world
> * '1,2' → Dungeon normal/heroic
> * '0,3' → Open world and Raid 10 Player
> * '3,4,5,6' → Raid 10/25 normal/heroic

columns.name: event_phase_mask
columns.label: Event phase mask
columns.hint: When dealing with phases, phase IDs have to be used.
columns.description:
When dealing with phases, phase IDs have to be used. There are 13 (12+1) different phases: 1, 2, ... 12 and the default 0.

Example: The script is in phase 0 by default - If we want it to go to phase 1, we got two choices:
 SMART_ACTION_INC_PHASE by 1 or SMART_ACTION_SET_PHASE 1

If the script is in phase 0 and want to skip to phase 2:
 SMART_ACTION_INC_PHASE by 2 or SMART_ACTION_SET_PHASE 2

If the script is in phase 1 and want to skip to phase 2:
 SMART_ACTION_INC_PHASE by 1 or SMART_ACTION_SET_PHASE 2

columns.name: event_chance
columns.label: Event chance
columns.hint: This is the probability of the event to occur as a percentage from 0-100.
columns.description: This is the probability of the event to occur as a percentage from 0-100. So, if you want the event to occur roughly half of the time, then set this to 50.

tables.name: spawn_group
tables.label: Spawn group
tables.description: This table contains Spawn Group members.

columns.name: spawnId
columns.label: Spawn Id
columns.hint: This is the guid of the creature/gameobject included in the group.
columns.description: This is the guid of the creature/gameobject included in the group.

tables.name: spawn_group_template
tables.label: Spawn group template
tables.description: This table contains Spawn Group names and flags. Spawn Groups are collections of creatures / gameobjects, linked to scripted events or boss fights.

columns.name: groupId
columns.label: Group Id
columns.hint: This is the ID for the group.
columns.description:
This is the ID for the group. It must be a unique number.
> Groups 0 – 4 are reserved for system tasks.

columns.name: groupName
columns.label: Group Name
columns.hint: This is a descriptive name for the group, like: [zone] - [related event] - [group content] e.g.: Halls of Lightning - General Bjarngrim - Stormforged Lieutenants
columns.description:
This is a descriptive name for the group, like: `[zone] - [related event] - [group content]`
e.g.: `Halls of Lightning - General Bjarngrim - Stormforged Lieutenants`

values.name: SPAWNGROUP_FLAG_DYNAMIC_SPAWN_RATE
values.comment: group is affected by config setting: Respawn.DynamicMode

values.name: SPAWNGROUP_FLAG_ESCORTQUESTNPC
values.comment: group is affected by config setting: Respawn.DynamicEscortNPC

tables.name: spell_area
tables.label: Spell area
tables.description: This table is used to apply a specific spell aura to the player within an area in the game. When any player enters this area or somehow interacts with a quest, this aura will be handled accordingly.

columns.name: spell
columns.label: Spell
columns.hint: The Spell ID to be casted on the player.
columns.description: The [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id) to be casted on the player.

columns.name: area
columns.label: Area
columns.hint: The AreaTable ID where spell should be applied.
columns.description: The [AreaTable ID](/files/DBC/335/areatable#id) where **spell** should be applied.

columns.name: quest_start
columns.label: Quest start
columns.hint: The Quest ID which the player must have in the state defined by quest_start_status for the spell to apply.
columns.description: The [Quest ID](../world/quest_template#id) which the player must have in the state defined by **quest_start_status** for the spell to apply.

columns.name: quest_end
columns.label: Quest end
columns.hint: The Quest ID which the player must not have in the state defined by quest_end_status for the spell to apply.
columns.description:
The [Quest ID](../world/quest_template#id) which the player must not have in the state defined by **quest_end_status** for the spell to apply.
Setting both quest_start and quest_end to the same value is useless.

columns.name: aura_spell
columns.label: Aura spell
columns.hint: If set, this value (plus or minus aura Spell ID) imposes additional condition.
columns.description:
If set, this value (plus or minus aura [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id)) imposes additional condition.
* **aura_spell** < 0: If the player has aura **-aura_spell** then **spell** will not be activated.
* **aura_spell** = 0: This column is ignored.
* **aura_spell** > 0: If the player has no aura **aura_spell** then **spell** will not be activated.

columns.name: racemask
columns.label: Racemask
columns.hint: Race mask of ChrRace IDs spell applies to.
columns.description: Race mask of [ChrRace IDs](/files/DBC/335/chrraces#id) **spell** applies to. (0: any race)

columns.name: gender
columns.label: Gender
columns.hint: The player gender this entry applies to.
columns.description:
The player gender this entry applies to.

[`enum Gender`](https://github.com/TrinityCore/TrinityCore/blob/3.3.5/src/server/shared/SharedDefines.h#L75-L80)

values.name: SPELL_AREA_FLAG_AUTOCAST
values.comment: If the spell should be automatically applied when the character enters the area. Also prevents the user from removing it.

values.name: SPELL_AREA_FLAG_AUTOREMOVE
values.comment: If the spell should be automatically removed when the character is inside the area (only works with quest updates)

values.name: QUEST_STATUS_NONE
values.comment: Player does not have or had quest at all. He could accept it, but he did not (yet).

values.name: QUEST_STATUS_COMPLETE
values.comment: Player fulfilled objectives, but did not hand it in yet.

values.name: QUEST_STATUS_INCOMPLETE
values.comment: Player did not fulfill objectives yet.

values.name: QUEST_STATUS_FAILED
values.comment: Player failed to fulfill objectives for any reason, e.g. time limit.

values.name: QUEST_STATUS_REWARDED
values.comment: Player handed quest in and this is sort of a post-quest interaction.

tables.name: spell_bonus_data
tables.label: Spell bonus data
tables.description: Table used for storing custom damage/healing bonus coefficients.

columns.name: entry
columns.label: Entry
columns.hint: references Spell ID Only the first rank of the spell needs data if spell exists in spell_ranks and coefficients are the same for each rank.
columns.description:
references [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id)
Only the first rank of the spell needs data if spell exists in [spell_ranks](../world/spell_ranks) and coefficients are the same for each rank.

columns.name: direct_bonus
columns.label: Direct bonus
columns.hint: Spell Power coefficient for the direct damage/healing component of the spell.
columns.description: Spell Power coefficient for the direct damage/healing component of the spell.

columns.name: dot_bonus
columns.label: Dot bonus
columns.hint: Spell Power coefficient for the over time component of the spell.
columns.description: Spell Power coefficient for the over time component of the spell.

columns.name: ap_bonus
columns.label: Ap bonus
columns.hint: Attack Power coefficient for the direct damage/healing component of the spell.
columns.description: Attack Power coefficient for the direct damage/healing component of the spell.

columns.name: ap_dot_bonus
columns.label: Ap dot bonus
columns.hint: Attack Power coefficient for the over time component of the spell.
columns.description:
Attack Power coefficient for the over time component of the spell.

#### for all fields:
* `0 <= bonus <= 1`: 0%  – 100% scaling
* `-1`: Uses generic scaling depending on cast time and aura duration.

columns.name: comments
columns.label: Comments
columns.hint: commonly: Spell User – Spell Name e.g.: Item - Onyxia 10 Caster Trinket - Searing Flames
columns.description:
commonly: Spell User – Spell Name
e.g.: `Item - Onyxia 10 Caster Trinket - Searing Flames`

tables.name: spell_custom_attr
tables.label: Spell custom attr
tables.description: Table used for storing custom spell attributes.

tables.name: spell_enchant_proc_data
tables.label: Spell enchant proc data
tables.description: This table holds information how and when an enchantment proc can occur.

columns.name: EnchantID
columns.label: Enchant ID
columns.hint: references SpellItemEnchantment ID Any of the types (0 – 2) must be of ITEM_ENCHANTMENT_TYPE_COMBAT_SPELL (1)
columns.description:
references [SpellItemEnchantment ID](/files/DBC/335/spellitemenchantment#id)
Any of the types (0 – 2) must be of ITEM_ENCHANTMENT_TYPE_COMBAT_SPELL (1)

columns.name: Chance
columns.label: Chance
columns.hint: Absolute chance per hit or spell cast.
columns.description: Absolute chance per hit or spell cast. (Used when **ProcsPerMinute** is 0)

columns.name: ProcsPerMinute
columns.label: Procs Per Minute
columns.hint: Chance relative to delay of equipped weapon .
columns.description:
Chance relative to [delay of equipped weapon](../world/item_template#delay) .
`chance = (ProcsPerMinute * delay) / 600`

columns.name: HitMask
columns.label: Hit Mask
columns.hint: Used to add special conditions to spells, some spells might trigger only on critical strikes, for example.
columns.description: Used to add special conditions to spells, some spells might trigger only on critical strikes, for example.

columns.name: AttributesMask
columns.label: Attributes Mask
columns.hint: Adds special behaviour to the proc, spell might trigger proc only if these conditions are fullfilled
columns.description: Adds special behaviour to the proc, spell might trigger proc only if these conditions are fullfilled

values.name: PROC_ATTR_REQ_EXP_OR_HONOR
values.comment: requires proc target to give exp or honor for aura proc

values.name: PROC_ATTR_TRIGGERED_CAN_PROC
values.comment: aura can proc even with triggered spells

values.name: PROC_ATTR_REQ_MANA_COST
values.comment: requires triggering spell to have a mana cost for aura proc

values.name: PROC_ATTR_REQ_SPELLMOD
values.comment: requires triggering spell to be affected by proccing aura to drop charges

values.name: PROC_ATTR_REDUCE_PROC_60
values.comment: aura should have a reduced chance to proc if level of proc Actor > 60

values.name: PROC_ATTR_CANT_PROC_FROM_ITEM_CAST
values.comment: do not allow aura proc if proc is caused by a spell casted by item

tables.name: spell_group
tables.label: Spell group
tables.description: Table used to group spells for various checks in the core. One spell may be added to many groups, but can occur in one group only once.

columns.name: id
columns.label: Id
columns.hint: Arbitrary ID defining a group of spells.
columns.description:
Arbitrary ID defining a group of spells. For custom made DB groups, it is required to be higher than 1000, as defined in SpellMgr.h.
> #define SPELL_GROUP_DB_RANGE_MIN 1000

columns.name: spell_id
columns.label: Spell id
columns.hint: spell_id > 0: Spell ID associated to this group.
columns.description:
* **spell_id** > 0: [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id) associated to this group. If the spell has multiple ranks it must be the [first_spell_id](/database/335/world/spell_ranks#first_spell_id).
* **spell_id** < 0: References another spell_group **id**.

tables.name: spell_group_stack_rules
tables.label: Spell group stack rules

columns.name: stack_rule
columns.label: Stack rule
columns.hint: Rule deciding which spell effect will prevail over the others as they are not stackable.

A spell should be in only 1 group with this stack rule.

values.name: SPELL_GROUP_STACK_RULE_EXCLUSIVE_FROM_SAME_CASTER

values.name: SPELL_GROUP_STACK_RULE_EXCLUSIVE_SAME_EFFECT

values.name: SPELL_GROUP_STACK_RULE_EXCLUSIVE_HIGHEST

auras of spell_effect are removed. | When the aura of spell_trigger is removed
auras of spell_effect are removed. | * 1: SPELL_LINK_HIT | -- | -- | -- | | | **spell_trigger > 0** | **spell_trigger < 0** | | **spell_effect > 0** | When spell_trigger hits it's target

aura of spell_effect is also applied on the same target. | *- invalid -* | | **spell_effect < 0** | While aura of spell_trigger is applied
target is immune to spell_effect. | *- invalid -* |

tables.name: spell_ranks
tables.label: Spell ranks
tables.description: Table used by the core to group different ranks of spells (the gray text seen on ranked spells) into one "spell stem". This partly involves checks for aura stacking (e.g. different levels of the same spell). One spell can not be linked to multiple rank chains (they are "unique").

columns.name: first_spell_id
columns.label: First spell id
columns.hint: Spell ID which is first rank of spell rank chain.
columns.description: [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id) which is first rank of spell rank chain. It identifies the whole chain.

columns.name: rank
columns.label: Rank
columns.hint: An integer which ranks the spell within the chain of spell ranks for the given spell_id.
columns.description:
An integer which ranks the spell within the chain of spell ranks for the given **spell_id**. It can differ from the rank text in game (for example, some ranks in client start with level 0, while the server always starts from level 1 onward).

Several conditions have to be fulfilled:
* At least two ranks are required.
* The ranking must be continuous (e.g. one spell being level 3 and one being level 5 while level 4 is missing altogether)
* There can be no duplicates in ranks.

Table is used also for profession specialisations as specialisations require profession of certain rank to learn.

tables.name: waypoint_data
tables.label: Waypoint data
tables.description: This table contains all the path data for creatures that use waypoints.

columns.name: id
columns.label: Id
columns.description:
Unique ID for each path.

The TDB standard way of assigning an ID is to multiply [creature guid](../world/creature#guid) by 10.

So for a creature with a GUID of 1234 the path ID would be 12340. Any waypoints submitted to TDB should follow this standard.

However, this is only a suggestion when creating your own waypoints. This ID can be anything you want as long as [path_id](../world/creature_addon#path_id) is set to the **id** you pick here for the creature you are creating a waypoint for.

columns.name: point
columns.label: Point
columns.hint: Unique point ID for each point in a path.
columns.description: Unique point ID for each point in a path. Starts at 1 and increases with each path node.

columns.name: position_x
columns.label: Position x
columns.hint: The X coordinate of the destination waypoint.
columns.description: The X coordinate of the destination waypoint.

columns.name: position_y
columns.label: Position y
columns.hint: The Y coordinate of the destination waypoint.
columns.description: The Y coordinate of the destination waypoint.

columns.name: position_z
columns.label: Position z
columns.hint: The Z coordinate of the destination waypoint.
columns.description: The Z coordinate of the destination waypoint.

columns.name: orientation
columns.label: Orientation
columns.description: The orientation of the creature. (North = 0.0; South = π (3.14159))

columns.name: delay
columns.label: Delay
columns.hint: Time to wait (in ms) before moving to the next point.
columns.description: Time to wait (in ms) before moving to the next point.

columns.name: action
columns.label: Action
columns.hint: Script ID of the action to be performed.
columns.description: [Script ID](../world/waypoint_scripts#id) of the action to be performed.

columns.name: wpguid
columns.label: Wpguid
columns.hint: This field is used by the core and is _NOT_ to be set by hand.
columns.description:
This field is used by the core and is _NOT_ to be set by hand.

This field holds the GUID of the waypoint visual when you enable the visual mode for waypoints.

columns.description:
Facing coordinate of the location **<u>in degrees</u>**

Note:
Radians to degrees: `Radians / (2 * PI() / 360)` (you can use this snippet in SQL)

Alternative in Python you can use this [gist](https://gist.github.com/TheSCREWEDSoftware/bc8655e5d91ffba418abd74c49281ed3).

columns.description:
MapIDs where the worldstate should be active (comma separated: `mapId1,mapId2`)
Using NULL as MapID means its active realmwide (= in every map).
Using -1 as MapID marks it as allowed on ALL maps but should be bound to a map.
References to: [Map.db2](https://wago.tools/db2/Map){target=_blank}

columns.name: AreaIDs

columns.hint: AreaIDs where the worldstate should be active (comma separated: areaId1,areaId2) Using NULL means its active in every area of the provided MapIDs.
